cards.title: Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016
cards.source: The Act may be cited as the Prescription Drug Monitoring Act of 2016. A covered state is one receiving federal prescription drug monitoring program funding. Beginning two years after enactment, each covered state must require prescribing practitioners, or authorized designees, to consult the state's prescription drug monitoring program before starting treatment with a controlled-substance prescription and at defined intervals afterward. Dispensers must report covered prescription information within the required time. The Department of Justice or Department of Health and Human Services may withhold grant funding from a state that fails to comply. A state must also share its monitoring-program data with other states through a data-sharing hub established by the Department of Justice, subject to privacy and security requirements.

cards.source: The Act may be cited as the Strategic Gasoline and Fuel Reserve Act of 2005. It directs the Secretary of Energy to establish, maintain, and operate a reserve separate from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The reserve may contain no more than 40,000,000 barrels of regular unleaded gasoline and 7,500,000 barrels of jet fuel. cards.source: The Act may be cited as the Special Agent Scott K. Carey Public Safety Officer Benefits Enhancement Act. records.title: Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016
records.source: The Act may be cited as the Fair Access to Investment Research Act of 2016. Within 45 days of enactment, the Securities and Exchange Commission shall propose, and within 180 days shall adopt, revisions to its rules creating a safe harbor for covered investment fund research reports published or distributed by brokers or dealers. A qualifying report is not treated as an offer for sale or an offer to sell a security covered by an effective registration statement, even when the broker or dealer participates in the offering. The report is treated as satisfying specified federal securities and self-regulatory organization conditions. In implementing the safe harbor, the SEC may not impose certain conditions based on whether a continuously offered fund report initiates or resumes coverage, and it must address appropriate disclosure and content standards for investor protection and capital formation.

Dispensers must report covered prescription information within the required time. A state must also share its monitoring-program data with other states through a data-sharing hub established by the Department of Justice, subject to privacy and security requirements.

records.title: Strategic Gasoline and Fuel Reserve Act of 2005
records.source: The Act may be cited as the Strategic Gasoline and Fuel Reserve Act of 2005. It directs the Secretary of Energy to establish, maintain, and operate a reserve separate from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The reserve may contain no more than 40,000,000 barrels of regular unleaded gasoline and 7,500,000 barrels of jet fuel. Within one year, the Secretary must choose at least three and no more than five regionally strategic sites; the sites must be operational within two years. The Secretary of Homeland Security must concur in physical and operational security. Fuel may be released only when the President finds a severe supply disruption or when a governor requests a release with specified findings. The bill establishes a revolving Strategic Gasoline and Fuel Reserve Fund in the Treasury.

It directs the Secretary of Energy to establish, maintain, and operate a reserve separate from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve. The reserve may contain no more than 40,000,000 barrels of regular unleaded gasoline and 7,500,000 barrels of jet fuel.
